images.title: Reading a triangle key
images.purpose: Show that each triangle stands for 10 children and a half triangle for 5.
images.composition: Key at the top, then two rows of triangles stacked with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Key at top: 1 triangle = 10 children. Row 1: exactly 5 teal #0072B2 triangles, labelled Always, then 5 × 10 = 50. Row 2: exactly 2 whole teal triangles then 1 half triangle in amber #E69F00 (left half filled), labelled Sometimes, then 20 + 5 = 25. All whole triangles the same size and evenly spaced. Exactly 2 rows, 7 whole triangles and 1 half.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a half triangle drawn as anything other than exactly half of a whole one
images.takeaway: Read the key first, then count in tens, and a half is 5.
images.description: A key line and two rows of triangles: 5 triangles make 50 children, and 2 triangles plus a half make 25.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to read the key aloud and then count each row in tens.

image_decisions.why: Reading a key and a half symbol is a picture idea; two short rows show it.
